title: XNDU Stock Rises On ASML Deal To Fix Photonic Quantum Chips' Optical Loss Problem
key_facts: Xanadu Quantum Technologies (XNDU), a Toronto photonic quantum computing company, announced a collaboration with chip-equipment maker ASML to develop lithography processes for its photonic quantum chips.
The work targets optical loss, signal weakening in the light-carrying waveguides, which Xanadu ties to line-edge roughness of the etched structures.
Xanadu shares rose 1.7 percent in pre-market trading on the Wednesday of the announcement; ASML fell as much as 2.7 percent in a weak market.
Xanadu uses photons for computation, unlike IonQ's trapped ions or IBM's superconducting circuits.
Earlier 2026 deals: EV Group (wafer bonding) and Mitsubishi Chemical (quantum algorithms for chip fabrication); a Toronto facility called Inception was announced last month.
Xanadu's August roadmap targets more than 1,000 logical (error-corrected) qubits by 2031.
quote_evidence: Xanadu said the collaboration focuses on reducing optical loss in the company’s photonic quantum computing chips.
"Fault tolerance and error correction are arguably the most important technical objectives for the quantum computing industry," said Christian Weedbrook, Xanadu’s founder and CEO.
XNDU stock rose 1.7% in pre-market trading and was among the top-trending tickers on Stocktwits.
why_it_matters_hint: Pairing with the world's main lithography supplier is about making photonic quantum chips manufacturable, but no results or timeline are given.
event_date: Article says Wednesday, most likely 30 Sep 2026; feed date 3 Oct 2026
notes: Stocktwits is a retail-trading news site; the article rests on Xanadu's own announcement. Internal dating (Wednesday) conflicts with the 3 Oct feed timestamp, so the event is probably 30 Sep 2026: treated as a follow-up. No financial terms, deliverables or timeline disclosed.
